At a summit in Montreal later this month (29-30 October), the EU and Canada will pledge to launch “an alliance for the future”, with a host of agreements on digital trade and the economy, and plans to intensify ties on raw materials, the Arctic and people-to-people contacts. The nine-page draft summit text seen by the Guardian does not mention the phrase “associate membership”, reflecting scepticism about the term European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen surprised EU diplomats with last month. Canada’s government also appeared to distance themselves from the term, which has no legal basis in EU treaties.
